title: ZPA client forwarding policy rules: actions, precedence and criteria

prose.text: {{sipa-rule-2}} The other rule is described differently by two pages {{divergence:sipa-rule-1-client-types}}. The Source IP Anchoring side is in [[zia.forwarding-control.sipa:client-forwarding-policy]].

prose.label: Names and limits.
prose.text: {{name-characters}} The rule limits are not stated {{gap:forwarding-limits}}.

checks.do: Check the rule action, since Bypass ZPA keeps the application off Private Access on all ports and wins over Forward to ZPA on another port.
If a blocked application's requests still reach the Private Service Edge under Only Forward Allowed Applications, check for a wildcard application segment that allows it.
For Source IP Anchoring forwarding rules, compare both pages' descriptions of the Bypass ZPA rule before choosing its client types.
If a rule combines client types and criteria, check the combinations the page rules out.

forwarding-purpose.statement: Client forwarding policy rules define when application requests are forwarded to Private Access from Zscaler Client Connector.

quotes: Client forwarding policy rules enable you to define when application requests are forwarded to Private Access (ZPA) from Zscaler Client Connector.

segment-bypass-takes-precedence.statement: For application segments, the Bypass setting takes precedence over any new client forwarding policy rule.

quotes: For application segments, the Bypass setting takes precedence over any new client forwarding policy rule.

bypass-zpa-action.statement: If Bypass ZPA is selected, applications are marked and bypassed for Private Access and Zscaler Client Connector does not send their requests to Private Access; the setting is the equivalent of Always for the Bypass setting within an application segment, and it is not port specific, so the applications are bypassed on all ports.

quotes: Bypass ZPA: If selected, applications are marked and bypassed for Private Access, and Zscaler Client Connector does not send application requests to Private Access.
This setting is the equivalent of selecting Always for the Bypass setting within an application segment.
The Bypass Private Access action is not port specific. When selected, applications are marked and bypassed for Private Access on all ports.

only-forward-allowed.statement: With Only Forward Allowed Applications, Zscaler Client Connector learns about and forwards traffic only for applications a user is allowed to access, a list the access policy determines and the service downloads to Client Connector when it sets up a connection to Private Access; requests for applications not on the list go out on the local network and are not logged in Private Access.

quotes: If you only want Zscaler Client Connector to learn about and forward traffic for applications that a user is allowed to access, select this action.
The list of applications that the user has access to is determined by the access policy.

When Zscaler Client Connector sets up a connection to Private Access, the service determines the list of applications that a user is allowed to access and only downloads this list to Zscaler Client Connector for forwarding traffic to Private Access.

For other applications that are not present on the list, Zscaler Client Connector forwards requests for them on the local network. So, requests for these applications are not logged in Private Access.

wildcard-example.statement: The page's example: when Only Forward Allowed Applications is set for a specific FQDN application segment (abc.example.com) whose access policy is Block, and a wildcard application segment (*.example.com) with an Allow access policy also exists, Client Connector still forwards traffic for abc.example.com to the Private Service Edge because it matches the wildcard domain, and the Private Service Edge then blocks the request under the more specific segment's block policy.

quotes: If a client forwarding policy is set to Only Forward Allowed Applications for a specific FQDN application segment (e.g., abc.example.com) with an access policy set to Block, and a wildcard application segment (e.g., *.example.com) with an access policy set to Allow also exists

Zscaler Client Connector still forwards traffic for abc.example.com to the Private Service Edge because it matches the wildcard domain. The Private Service Edge then blocks the request based on the more specific FQDN application segment's block policy.

forward-to-zpa.statement: If Forward to ZPA is selected, Zscaler Client Connector forwards application requests to Private Access, including requests to applications the user is not authorized to access; it is selected by default.

quotes: Forward to ZPA: If selected, Zscaler Client Connector forwards application requests to Private Access. This includes requests to applications that the user is not authorized to access. This is selected by default.

bypass-beats-forward-on-ports.statement: If there are multiple client forwarding policies with both Bypass ZPA and Forward to ZPA rules for a given domain with different ports, the Bypass ZPA rule action takes precedence.

quotes: If you have multiple client forwarding policies with both Bypass ZPA and Forward to ZPA rules for a given domain with different ports, the Bypass ZPA rule action takes precedence.

sipa-rule-2.statement: For Source IP Anchoring, the client forwarding page's Rule 2 for domain-based applications enables the Forward to ZPA rule action for both Segment Groups and Client Types > ZIA Service Edge.

quotes: Rule 2: Enable the Forward to ZPA rule action for both Segment Groups and Client Types > ZIA Service Edge.

criteria-list.statement: The client forwarding rule criteria cover SAML or SCIM criteria, an external IAM IdP, application segments and segment groups, Branch Connector groups, Client Connector Posture Profile condition sets, trusted networks, client types, Cloud Connector groups, Machine groups and platforms.

quotes: To use SAML or SCIM Criteria:
To use External IAM IdP, select the IdP from the drop-down menu.
Choose the application segments and segment groups to which this rule applies:
Choose the Branch Connector groups to which the rule applies.
You can add up to 10 Client Connector Posture Profile condition sets to the rule.
Choose the trusted networks to which the rule applies, and click Done.
Choose the client types to which the rule applies, and click Done.
The Cloud Connector Group criteria type cannot be configured with the SAML and SCIM Attributes criteria type.
If a Machine group is selected, Machine Tunnel as a client type is required as well.
Choose the platforms to which the rule applies and click Save.

criteria-combinations.statement: On the client forwarding page the Cloud Connector Group criteria type cannot be configured with the SAML and SCIM Attributes criteria type, multiple Cloud Connector groups are joined by an AND Boolean operator, and a selected Machine group requires Machine Tunnel as a client type.

quotes: The Cloud Connector Group criteria type cannot be configured with the SAML and SCIM Attributes criteria type.
If you've added multiple Cloud Connector groups to the policy rule, Private Access uses an AND Boolean operator between them.
If a Machine group is selected, Machine Tunnel as a client type is required as well.

client-types.statement: The client types listed for a client forwarding rule are Branch Connector, Client Connector, Cloud Browser, Machine Tunnel, Web Browser and ZIA Service Edge, and rules using the Web Browser or ZIA Service Edge client types cannot also use the posture profiles or trusted networks criteria.

quotes: Branch Connector: To learn more, see About Branch Connectors.
Client Connector: To learn more, see What Is Zscaler Client Connector?
Cloud Browser: To learn more, see About Cloud Browser Isolation.
Machine Tunnel: To learn more, see About Machine Tunnels.
Web Browser: To learn more, see About Browser Access.
ZIA Service Edge: To learn more, see About Source IP Anchoring.
Rules using the Web Browser or ZIA Service Edge client types can not also use posture profiles or trusted networks criteria.

trusted-network-delegation.statement: The page says client forwarding policies must delegate each app profile to its intended trusted network.

quotes: Client forwarding policies must delegate each app profile to its intended trusted network.

trusted-network-client-version.statement: The page says users must be running Zscaler Client Connector version 2.1.0 to apply the trusted networks criterion to a policy rule.

quotes: Choose the trusted networks to which the rule applies, and click Done.
Your users must be running Zscaler Client Connector version 2.1.0 to apply this criteria to your policy rule.

name-characters.statement: A client forwarding rule name cannot contain special characters except periods, hyphens and underscores.

quotes: Name: Enter a client forwarding policy name. The name cannot contain special characters, except for periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).

sipa-rule-1-client-types.summary: The Source IP Anchoring configuring page and the client forwarding page describe Rule 1, the Bypass ZPA rule for domain-based applications, with different client types, and scope the IP address-based rule differently.

quotes: Rule 1: Select the Bypass ZPA rule action for Source IP Anchoring Segment Groups and add all client types, except ZIA Service Edge client type.
For IP address-based applications, select the Only Forward Allowed Applications rule action for Source IP Anchoring application segments.

positions.says: Rule 1 bypasses for the Source IP Anchoring segment groups with all client types except ZIA Service Edge, and the IP address-based rule is scoped to Source IP Anchoring application segments.

quotes: Rule 1: Enable the Bypass ZPA rule action for both Segment Groups and Client Types > Client Connector.
For IP address-based applications, select the Only Forward Allowed Applications rule action for Source IP Anchoring segment groups.

positions.says: Rule 1 bypasses for Segment Groups and the Client Connector client type, and the IP address-based rule is scoped to Source IP Anchoring segment groups.

sipa-rule-1-client-types.impact: Following one page gives a Rule 1 for every client type except ZIA Service Edge, and following the other gives one for Client Connector only; the pages also differ on whether the IP address-based rule names application segments or segment groups.

forwarding-limits.title: The limits on client forwarding rules
forwarding-limits.detail: The captured page states no client forwarding rule limits, and it does not map the three console actions to BYPASS, INTERCEPT and INTERCEPT_ACCESSIBLE (see zpa.policy.actions).
